questions.question: The more you take away from me, the larger I become. What am I?
I can be broken without being touched, given without being held, and kept without being locked away. What am I?
I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, and rivers but no water. What am I?
I speak without a mouth and hear without ears. I have no body, but I come alive when something calls me. What am I?
What belongs to you, but other people use it more often than you do?
I am always ahead of you, but you can never see me. What am I?
What can travel around the world while remaining in one corner?
I have keys but no locks, space but no room, and you can enter but cannot go inside. What am I?
The person who makes me does not need me. The person who buys me does not use me. The person who uses me does not know it. What am I?
I become shorter as I grow older, and I give light while slowly disappearing. What am I?
What disappears the moment you say its name?
I am not alive, but I grow. I have no lungs, but I need air. Water kills me. What am I?
What gets wetter the more it dries?
A man looks at a photograph and says, 'Brothers and sisters, I have none, but that man's father is my father's son.' Who is in the photograph?
A woman has four daughters, and each daughter has one brother. How many children does the woman have?
What has many teeth but cannot bite?
What can fill an entire room but takes up no physical space?
I have a neck but no head, two arms but no hands. What am I?
What can you hold in your left hand but never in your right hand?
I have no life, yet I can die. I have no mouth, yet I can be fed. What am I?
What does the proverb 'A bird in the hand is worth two in the bush' teach?

options.B: Having something certain is better than risking it for something greater but uncertain
options.C: One should always hunt for more

questions.question: What is the meaning of 'When two elephants fight, it is the grass that suffers'?

options.C: Conflicts between powerful people often harm innocent or weaker people

questions.question: What does 'A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step' emphasise?

options.A: Great achievements begin with small actions

questions.question: What is implied by the saying 'Empty vessels make the most noise'?

options.B: People who speak loudly are always correct
options.C: Silence is a sign of weakness
options.D: People with little knowledge often talk the most confidently

questions.question: What does 'Do not count your chickens before they hatch' warn against?

options.B: Assuming success before it has actually happened

questions.question: What is the lesson in 'You reap what you sow'?

options.C: Your actions determine the consequences you experience

questions.question: What does 'The axe forgets, but the tree remembers' suggest?

options.A: Those who cause harm may forget, but those harmed may remember
options.B: Trees are more intelligent than people

questions.question: What does 'A chain is only as strong as its weakest link' mean?

options.C: Weakness is always easy to identify
options.D: The weakness of one part can undermine the whole group

questions.question: What is the meaning of 'He who asks is a fool for five minutes, but he who does not ask remains a fool forever'?

options.A: Questions should only be asked in school
options.B: Asking questions is a way to overcome ignorance

questions.question: What does 'Make hay while the sun shines' advise?

options.C: Take advantage of favourable opportunities while they last

questions.question: What does 'The early bird catches the worm' communicate?

options.A: Being prompt and prepared can create advantages
options.B: Birds should wake up before sunrise
options.C: Success comes only to the strongest

questions.question: What is the meaning of 'Too many cooks spoil the broth'?

options.C: Large teams always produce better results
options.D: Too many people interfering in one task can damage the outcome

questions.question: What does 'A fool and his money are soon parted' warn about?

options.B: Careless or unwise people can easily lose their money

questions.question: What is meant by 'The grass is always greener on the other side'?

options.A: Other people's circumstances may appear better than our own

questions.question: What does 'One rotten apple spoils the barrel' suggest?

options.A: Fruit should be stored in cold places
options.C: One bad influence can negatively affect an entire group

questions.question: What is the lesson behind 'Actions speak louder than words'?

options.A: Speaking is more important than listening
options.D: What people do is more convincing than what they claim

questions.question: What does 'You cannot teach an old dog new tricks' traditionally suggest?

options.B: People may find it difficult to change established habits
options.D: Education is only for young people

questions.question: What is the meaning of 'A rising tide lifts all boats'?

options.A: Improvement in general conditions can benefit many people

questions.question: What does 'The tongue has no bones, but it is strong enough to break a heart' remind us?

options.C: Words can cause serious emotional harm

questions.question: What does 'If you want to go fast, go alone; if you want to go far, go together' emphasise?

options.B: Working together is important for lasting achievements
options.C: Speed is the only measure of success

questions.question: Which philosopher is traditionally associated with the statement 'The unexamined life is not worth living'?
Which philosopher is associated with the statement 'I think, therefore I am'?
A person tells the truth even though lying would help them avoid punishment. Which value are they demonstrating?
A government makes a law that is legal but treats one group unfairly. What philosophical issue does this raise?

options.A: Whether laws should be written down
options.B: Whether all citizens should have the same jobs
options.D: Whether something legal is necessarily just

questions.question: A person helps a stranger in need without expecting money, praise or a reward. What principle best describes this action?
Why should people question information before accepting it as true?

options.B: Because opinions are always better than facts
options.C: Because claims may be mistaken and should be tested with evidence and reason
options.D: Because questioning everything makes a person an expert

questions.question: A judge gives the same fair treatment to a rich person and a poor person facing the same charge. Which idea is being demonstrated?
Someone does a good deed only because they are afraid of being punished if they do not. What question does this raise about their action?

options.D: Whether the action came from genuine moral conviction

questions.question: What is the main difference between knowledge and a mere opinion?

options.B: Knowledge is supported by adequate reasons or evidence

questions.question: A decision will make most people happy but will seriously harm a small minority. Which ethical problem does this illustrate?

options.B: Whether the majority is always correct
options.C: Whether the greatest overall benefit justifies harm to a minority
options.D: Whether people should avoid making decisions

questions.question: If people are free to choose their actions, what important idea is often linked to that freedom?

options.A: Responsibility for the consequences of their choices
options.C: The right to control other people
options.D: The belief that choices do not matter

questions.question: A person changes their opinion after discovering strong evidence that their original belief was wrong. What quality are they showing?
A speaker claims that an idea must be correct because millions of people believe it. What is the weakness in this argument?

options.B: Popularity alone does not prove that a claim is true
options.D: It asks the audience to think

questions.question: Can an action be legal but still be morally wrong?

options.A: No, law and morality always mean exactly the same thing
options.B: Only if the action is unpopular
options.C: Yes, because legality and morality are not always identical
options.D: Only when no one witnesses it

questions.question: A student refuses to cheat in an examination even though nobody would discover it. What does this best demonstrate?
Which branch of philosophy asks fundamental questions about what exists and the nature of reality?
Two witnesses observe the same event but remember it differently. What does this situation remind us?

options.A: One witness must always be lying
options.B: Human knowledge and memory can be influenced by perspective
options.D: The truth is always decided by the majority

questions.question: A person chooses to forgive someone who has wronged them instead of seeking revenge. Which idea does this choice reflect?

options.B: The belief that wrongdoing should be ignored
options.C: A moral response that may break the cycle of hostility
options.D: The claim that justice is unnecessary

questions.question: What does critical thinking mainly require a person to do?

options.A: Examine ideas, question assumptions and evaluate evidence
options.B: Accept the first explanation they hear
options.C: Agree with the most confident speaker

questions.question: A person has wealth and comfort but is not free to make important choices about their own life. What philosophical question does this situation raise?

options.C: Whether every person should become famous
options.D: What makes a human life meaningful and worth living
